propositions.text: The claimant is a Venezuelan citizen claiming protection under IRPA sections 96, 97(1)(a), and 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, a citizen of Venezuela, is claiming protection in Canada under section 96 and paragraphs 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a Venezuelan citizen, claims protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b).

propositions.text: This paragraph summarizes the claimant's allegations from his Personal Information Form (PIF).
propositions.quote: This is a summary of the claimant's allegations, as they appear in his Personal Information Form (PIF).

paragraphs.summary: The paragraph summarizes the claimant's allegations from his Personal Information Form.

propositions.text: The claimant's brother was an anti-Chavez political activist who collected incriminating evidence against a former mayor.
propositions.quote: The claimant, who was living in XXXXX, had a brother, XXXXX, who was an anti-Chavez political activist. His brother had gathered on diskette some incriminating evidence of corruption concerning the former mayor of XXXXX in XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his brother was an anti-Chavez activist who collected incriminating evidence against a former mayor.

propositions.text: The claimant's brother gave him the diskette before fleeing Venezuela in 2006 due to threats.
propositions.quote: Feeling as though his life was threatened, XXXXX gave this diskette to the claimant before he left for Canada in 2006.

propositions.text: In 2009, a journalist investigating embezzlement contacted the claimant's mother about the evidence.
propositions.quote: In 2009, the claimant's mother was visited by a journalist who was investigating embezzlement by the former mayor of XXXXX. She told the claimant's mother that she knew that this evidence existed.

propositions.text: The former mayor was formally charged with corruption in 2009.
propositions.quote: The former mayor was formally charged with XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX in XXXXX 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's brother gave him the diskette before fleeing; a journalist contacted his mother about the evidence; the former mayor was charged in 2009.

propositions.text: In 2009, the Bolivarian Militia entered the claimant's mother's home searching for him and his brother.
propositions.quote: When the claimant was in Canada in XXXXX 2009, he found out that the Bolivarian Militia had entered his mother's home looking for him and XXXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant's stepfather was stopped on the premises and later found murdered on a public roadway.
propositions.quote: The claimant's stepfather, who lived with his mother, was stopped on the premises and was found murdered on the public roadway.

propositions.text: A threatening note about the claimant and his brother was found in the claimant's mother's home, and she filed a police complaint.
propositions.quote: A threatening note regarding the claimant and XXXXX was found in the claimant's mother's home. She filed a complaint with the police.

paragraphs.summary: The Bolivarian Militia searched the claimant's mother's home; the stepfather was murdered; a threatening note was found and a police complaint filed.

propositions.text: The claimant voluntarily returned to Venezuela in 2009 and gave the diskettes to the journalist.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXX, 2009, the claimant returned voluntarily to Venezuela. He returned the diskettes to the journalist who had come to see his mother previously.

propositions.text: The journalist advised the claimant to file a complaint with the attorney general's office, noting government control.
propositions.quote: The journalist told the claimant that the government was controlling everything but advised him to file a complaint to the office of the attorney general.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant returned to Venezuela in 2009, gave the diskettes to a journalist, who advised him to file a complaint with the attorney general.

propositions.text: The claimant filed a complaint with the attorney general's office in 2009 and moved frequently with his family.
propositions.quote: On XXXXXX, 2009, the claimant filed a complaint there. He moved from home to home with his family.

propositions.text: He learned from lawyer friends that he was listed as a traitor by the government.
propositions.quote: He learned from lawyer friends that his name was on file in a database of people considered to be traitors by the government.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant filed a complaint in 2009, moved frequently, and learned he was labeled a government traitor.

propositions.text: The claimant left Venezuela and arrived in Canada in 2010, claiming refugee protection.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2010, the claimant left Venezuela and arrived in Canada the same day; he claimed refugee protection there.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant left Venezuela and claimed refugee protection in Canada in 2010.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity, established by exhibits including his passport.
propositions.quote: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity, which was established by means of the exhibits submitted on file, especially his passport.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's identity established by exhibits, especially his passport.

propositions.text: The panel concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection after reviewing evidence.
propositions.quote: After reviewing the documentary and testimonial evidence, the panel concludes that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection after reviewing evidence.

propositions.text: The claimant is not credible.
propositions.quote: The claimant is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant not credible.

propositions.text: The claimant denied his brother's political activism multiple times when questioned by the panel.
propositions.quote: When asked whether the claimant's brother XXXXX had been involved in political activities, the claimant responded that he had not and added that this brother worked for the XXXXXXXXXXX in the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not know if his brother was involved in other political or social activities.
propositions.quote: He added that he did not know whether his brother XXXXX was involved in other political activities.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant denied his brother's political activism multiple times and said he did not know if his brother was involved in other political activities.

propositions.text: The claimant contradicted his PIF by later admitting his brother was an opposition activist, claiming misunderstanding the question.
propositions.quote: The panel told the claimant that he had written in the second paragraph of question 31 of his PIF that his brother XXXXX was [translation] "an activist who opposed the ruling regime in Venezuela." The claimant then did an about-face and stated that his brother was part of the opposition and that he had not understood the question correctly.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant contradicted his PIF by admitting his brother was an opposition activist, claiming he misunderstood the question.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation as unsatisfactory and notes he did not indicate misunderstanding the question.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects this explanation because it is not satisfactory. The panel asked the question more than once; the question was not complex, and the claimant did not indicate that he did not understand it even though the panel had informed the claimant in its instructions at the beginning of the hearing that if he did not understand a question, he had to inform the panel.

propositions.text: The claimant is educated and cognitively capable, undermining his explanation for denying his brother's activism.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant does not have any intellectual and cognitive deficiencies-he is an educated person, is XXXXXXXX, and was the XXXXXXXXXXXXXX where he was responsible for XXXX employees, which indicates that his abilities are at the very least average.

propositions.text: The panel believes the claimant would not have denied his brother's activism if true, undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: Rather, the panel is of the opinion that if the claimant's brother, XXXXX, had really been an anti-Chavez political activist and that if the claimant had suffered for that reason, he would not have spontaneously said no on more than one occasion, and he would not have contradicted question 31 of his PIF by stating that he did not think that his brother XXXXX was involved in anti-governmental political activism.

propositions.text: This contradiction significantly undermines the claimant's credibility as his claim is based on his brother's activism.
propositions.quote: All of this undermines his credibility significantly given that the claimant's refugee protection claim is based on his brother XXXX's anti-governmental political activism.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation, noting his education and contradictions undermine his credibility regarding his brother's activism.

propositions.text: The claimant stated he feared being killed since 2009 after his mother's spouse was allegedly killed during an armed group's visit.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he had been afraid of being killed since XXXXX 2009, when his mother's spouse, Mr. XXXXX, had allegedly been killed. He added that this took place on XXXXX, 2009, when an armed group went to his mother's home.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant stated he feared being killed since 2009 after his mother's spouse was allegedly killed during an armed group's visit.

propositions.text: The claimant initially said he did not know the armed group's name, then said it was the Bolivarian Circles, explaining misunderstanding the question.
propositions.quote: When asked what the name of this armed group was, the claimant stated that he did not know the name of this group. Then, after a moment, he stated that it was the Bolivarian Circles. When asked why he had responded that he did not know the name of this group, the claimant stated that he had understood from the question that he was being asked for the names of each person in this group.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant first said he did not know the armed group's name, then said Bolivarian Circles, explaining he misunderstood the question.

propositions.text: The claimant said Bolivarian Circles and Bolivarian Militia are the same, differing by uniform or civilian clothing.
propositions.quote: When asked why the claimant had stated that it was the Bolivarian Circles who had gone to his mother's home and not the Bolivarian Militia, as he had written in question 31 of his PIF, the claimant stated that it was the same thing. He then added that when they are in uniform, they are called Bolivarian Militia, and when they are in civilian clothing, they are called Bolivarian Circle.

propositions.text: The claimant said they were in uniform at his mother's home but mistakenly said Bolivarian Circle during testimony.
propositions.quote: Then, the claimant stated that they had been in uniform at his mother's home. He added: [translation] "I wrote Bolivarian Militia, but when I spoke, I became confused when I stated Bolivarian Circle."

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said Bolivarian Circles and Militia are the same, differing by clothing; he was confused in testimony about which group visited.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's testimony about the armed group vague, confused, and contradictory.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant's testimony about the question of the Bolivarian Circles or Bolivarian Militia who allegedly went to the claimant's mother's home on XXXXXX, 2009, is vague, confused and contradictory.

propositions.text: The claimant contradicted himself about the group's name and knowledge of it, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he did not know the name of the group that went to his mother's home, and then he stated that it was the Bolivarian Circle, whereas in his PIF, it is written that it was the Bolivarian Militia.

propositions.text: If the claimant truly knew about the group's visit and feared murder, he would not have contradicted himself about the group's identity.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that if the claimant had really learned from his mother (when he was in Calgary, in Canada) that on XXXXXX, 2009, the Bolivarian Circles had gone to her home armed, threatening, and looking for the claimant and his brother XXXXX, and that if, according to his testimony, this visit had caused the claimant to be so afraid that since that day, he is afraid of being murdered, the claimant would not have contradicted himself concerning the identity of this group when he knew the difference between the two, and he also would not have stated that he did not know the name of this group.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant failed to establish a link between his stepfather's death and his or his brother's problems.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that he failed to establish that the death of his stepfather was related to the claimant's and his brother XXXXX problems.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's testimony about the armed group vague and contradictory, undermining credibility and failing to link stepfather's death to claimant's problems.

propositions.text: The claimant initially said the armed group visited twice, then corrected to once, blaming nervousness and confusion.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the claimant stated that this Bolivarian Circles group went to his mother's home twice-on XXXXX and XXXXX, 2009. The claimant then stated that this was not correct and that the Bolivarian Circles had only gone to his mother's home once, on XXXXX, 2009. He stated that he was nervous, that it was the first time that he had testified before a panel, and that he had gotten confused.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant first said the armed group visited twice, then corrected to once, blaming nervousness and confusion.

propositions.text: The panel finds nervousness does not explain the claimant's changing testimony about the armed group's visits and stepfather's murder.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that this nervousness did not explain why the claimant changed his testimony. First, he stated that the Bolivarian Circles had killed his stepfather on XXXXX, 2009, when they went to the claimant's mother's home, but then he stated that they had in fact gone twice, indicating that it was during the second visit-on XXXXX, 2009-that the murder took place. He then retracted these facts and stated that it was only on XXXXX that the Bolivarian Circles had come.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds nervousness does not explain the claimant's inconsistent testimony about the armed group's visits and stepfather's murder.

propositions.text: The panel attaches no credibility to the 2009 incidents involving the claimant's mother's spouse's death.
propositions.quote: the panel attaches no credibility to the XXXXX, 2009, incidents

propositions.text: The panel is not convinced the death was related to the claimant's and his brother's problems.
propositions.quote: the panel is not of the opinion that this death was related to the claimant's and his brother XXXXX's problems

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no credibility in the 2009 incidents and does not believe the death relates to the claimant's or brother's problems.

propositions.text: The claimant stated his spouse and children have been hiding since 2010 in a location eight hours from the capital.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that his spouse and XXX children have been hiding since XXXXX, 2010, in XXXXXX, in the state of XXXXXX, which is eight hours from the capital

propositions.text: The claimant explained he wrote the wrong address on his PIF because he thought he had to write their address.
propositions.quote: he responded that he had thought that he had to write their address

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation as not credible and finds it inconsistent with other family address details provided.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects this explanation because it is not credible

propositions.text: The panel believes the claimant would have indicated his immediate family's hiding if true, or corrected the PIF later.
propositions.quote: if the claimant's immediate family had really been living in hiding since XXXXX 2009, he would have indicated this in question 4 of his PIF, or if there had been a mistake, he would have subsequently corrected it

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says his family has been hiding since 2010 but gave an incredible explanation for address inconsistencies; the panel rejects his credibility.

propositions.text: The claimant said he filed two complaints to authorities in 2009 and 2010.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he filed two complaints to the authorities-one on XXXXXX, 2009, in XXXXX, and the other in XXXXX 2010, in XXXXX

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not know why he wrote only one complaint in his PIF.
propositions.quote: the claimant responded that maybe at the time he had not mentioned it and that he did not know why he had not mentioned it

paragraphs.summary: The claimant says he filed two complaints but admitted he did not mention both in his PIF and did not know why.

propositions.text: The claimant stated he filed a complaint in 2009 in a city but wrote in his PIF he left for another city that year.
propositions.quote: the claimant stated that he had filed a complaint in XXXXXX on XXXXXX, 2009, when he had written in his PIF that on XXXXXX, 2009, he had left for XXXXX

propositions.text: The claimant hesitated and seemed confused when questioned about travel and complaint filing dates.
propositions.quote: the claimant hesitated and seemed confused

propositions.text: The claimant said he forgot to specify returning to a city and omitted some details in his PIF.
propositions.quote: maybe he had forgotten that and that maybe he had not mentioned a few details in his PIF

propositions.text: The claimant's counsel asked the panel to consider a PIF paragraph about moving homes and families.
propositions.quote: The claimant's counsel asked the panel to consider paragraph four of page four of question 31 of the PIF

propositions.text: The panel finds the PIF paragraph does not specify dates or locations of moves and notes the claimant left for a city on a specific date.
propositions.quote: this paragraph does not specify the dates or the locations of the claimant's and his family's moves

propositions.text: The panel finds it unlikely the claimant would not specify a flight to file a complaint in his PIF if it had occurred.
propositions.quote: if, according to his testimony, the claimant had taken the airplane in the following days in order to go to XXXXXX to file a complaint there, he would have made the effort to specify it in his PIF

paragraphs.summary: The claimant gave inconsistent testimony about complaint filing and travel; the panel finds his PIF lacks expected details and doubts his account.

propositions.text: The claimant explained no corroborating documents exist because complaints against politicians are verbal and confidential.
propositions.quote: when you file a complaint against a politician, there is a special division at the office of the attorney general... you can only file verbal complaints, thus ensuring the confidentiality

propositions.text: The claimant said police receive complaints in writing despite the special division's confidentiality.
propositions.quote: the police officer who receives the complaint receives it in writing

propositions.text: The claimant said his lawyers told him no corroborative evidence exists due to the special division's nature.
propositions.quote: his lawyers told him that there was no corroborative evidence for his complaints given that the nature of this special division was to provide no copy or corroborating document

paragraphs.summary: The claimant explained no evidence exists for complaints due to a special confidential division and lawyers' advice.

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not think to ask his lawyers for a document about inability to obtain evidence.
propositions.quote: the claimant stated that he had not thought of that

propositions.text: The panel finds it implausible the claimant did not ask lawyers for a letter explaining lack of evidence.
propositions.quote: if the claimant had really asked his lawyers to find him corroborative evidence... he would have thought to submit a letter from his lawyers

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's explanation about the special division and confidentiality not credible and unsupported by evidence.
propositions.quote: it seems implausible to the panel that there would be a special division... no document is received in order to ensure confidentiality

propositions.text: The panel finds no corroboration in documentary evidence and doubts the claimant's credibility about filing complaints.
propositions.quote: The panel finds nothing to corroborate this in the documentary evidence... All of this does not seem credible and undermines the claimant's credibility

propositions.text: The panel does not consider that the claimant filed a complaint with the police.
propositions.quote: The panel does not consider that the claimant filed a complaint with the police

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's explanations about complaints and confidentiality not credible and concludes he did not file police complaints.

propositions.text: The claimant feared murder by associates since 2009 after learning of his stepfather's murder and home intrusion.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he had been afraid of being murdered by XXXXXXXXX and his associates since XXXXX 2009

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not claim refugee protection in 2009 because he was unaware of the seriousness then.
propositions.quote: he was not aware of the seriousness of the matter

propositions.text: The claimant said visiting his brother in Canada and returning to Venezuela might have helped solve the problem.
propositions.quote: coming to speak with his brother in Canada and then returning to XXXXXX, which he did in XXXXXX 2009, could have helped him solve the problem

propositions.text: The claimant said filing a report might have enabled government action and he led a normal life before problems.
propositions.quote: maybe just filing a report would have enabled the government to do something. He added that he led a normal life in Venezuela before his problems began

paragraphs.summary: The claimant feared murder since 2009 but delayed refugee claim, hoping family visits and reports would help, and said he lived normally before.

propositions.text: The panel finds that if the claimant had learned of aggressive threats and his stepfather's murder, he would have sought protection in Canada.
propositions.quote: if the claimant had really learned that the Bolivarian Circle was looking for him aggressively... he would have sought protection in Canada

propositions.text: The panel does not accept the claimant's explanation that he returned to Venezuela to care for family, doubting the family's hiding claim.
propositions.quote: the panel does not accept the claimant's additional explanation that he wanted to return to Venezuela in order to take care of his family, because the panel does not believe that this family is living in hiding

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant would have sought protection if threatened and rejects his explanation about returning to care for family.

propositions.text: The claimant did not establish to the panel's satisfaction the elements supporting his fear.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not establish to the panel's satisfaction the alleged elements to support his fear

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant failed to establish elements supporting his fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's counsel requested extension to submit documents on political activism and lawyer's letter about evidence.
propositions.quote: the claimant's counsel requested an extension in order to submit documents on the political activism... as well as a letter from the claimant's lawyer

propositions.text: The panel received documents P-8 to P-10 and P-83 but attaches no probative value to P-83 letter from Venezuelan lawyer.
propositions.quote: the panel received documents, accepted under P-8 to P-10; P-83 is a letter from a lawyer in Venezuela. The panel attaches no probative value to this document

propositions.text: The panel notes the letter lacks letterhead or address, which undermines its credibility.
propositions.quote: this document does not contain a letterhead or address, which in itself seems contradictory

propositions.text: The panel previously found the claimant not credible and thus does not attach probative value to the document.
propositions.quote: the panel indicated previously that in its opinion, the claimant is not credible. Therefore, the panel does not attach probative value to this document

paragraphs.summary: The panel received documents but finds the lawyer's letter not credible and attaches no probative value due to claimant's lack of credibility.

propositions.text: The panel reviewed news clippings but finds them irrelevant due to claimant's lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: because it found that the claimant was not credible, these news clippings are not relevant to the panel's decision

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds news clippings irrelevant because the claimant is not credible.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the claimant... is not a "Convention refugee" or "person in need of protection"

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The claimant's refugee protection claim in Canada is rejected.
propositions.quote: his refugee protection claim in Canada is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's refugee protection claim in Canada.
